Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — Performance targets & SLO follow-up

Ben — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we have alignment before I loop in procurement/engineering for the sizing POC.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Workload: customer-facing chat assistant + batch reranking for personalization. Typical prompt sizes average ~350 tokens; worst-case sequences ~2,048 tokens.
- Current traffic: expected steady-state of 120 QPS for chat (peak concurrency ~20 active streamed sessions) and up to 10 batch reranks / min (each 1-2k tokens).
- SLO targets: first-token latency for streaming < 150ms p95, sustained per-token latency target to keep user-perceived latency under 300ms for typical responses, and availability 99.9%.
- Constraint: procurement timeline ~Q3 end; budget sensitivity to reserved capacity monthly commit.

What we propose (next steps)
1) Dev to validate GPU mix & reserved throughput sizing for your SLOs and give a recommended Dedicated pool config (H100 vs A100 vs mixed).
2) Run a short POC (2 weeks) with synthetic traffic matching your token distributions to validate p95 first-token and sustained token throughput.
3) Deliver a finalized cost/throughput tradeoff and a mutual action plan for procurement + contract terms.

Attachments: initial sizing worksheet + GPU benchmark summary attached for reference.
Links: HubSpot deal RW-4521 (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/RW-4521) and our shared drive folder with the call recording.

Action: Can you confirm the peak concurrency number (20) is correct and whether you need strict streaming-first-token p95 at 150ms or if 200ms is acceptable for the first phase? Also confirm whether on-prem (VPC) deployment is required or cloud-managed Dedicated is fine.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers from our side:
- Peak concurrency: 18-22 active streaming sessions (we'll plan for 22 headroom).
- Average prompt size: 350 tokens; heavy tails to 2,048.
- Streaming requirement: first-token p95 target is 150ms for GA; 200ms acceptable during an initial POC if it helps with cost tradeoffs.
- Availability: 99.9% SLA required for production.
- Deployment: cloud-managed Dedicated is preferred (VPC access is required, but we do not need fully on-prem infrastructure).

Procurement note: procurement will need a cost estimate and a short POC plan to greenlight the reserved commit. We can start the POC in early July if we get the design and test harness this week.

Thanks — Ben

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Howard <ben.howard@shopwell.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — Performance targets & SLO follow-up

Ben — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs plus a preliminary sizing recommendation based on your targets.

Clarifying questions:
- Are your streamed responses typically returned as many small chunks (token-by-token) or as occasional larger chunks? That affects first-byte vs inter-token latency behavior.
- For batch reranks, what's the typical model size (params) you want to run? (e.g., 7B, 13B, 70B).
- Do you plan to enable KV cache reuse for repeated conversational sessions?

Preliminary sizing notes (assumptions: model ~13B quantized INT8, average response 350 tokens, peak concurrency 22 streaming sessions, worst-case seq length 2,048 for a small subset):
- Recommendation: H100-backed Dedicated pool for the streaming-critical front-end. H100 gives better single-stream latency & token throughput vs A100 for high parallelism; A100 is more cost-efficient for batch-only workloads.
- Mixed pool option: 60% H100 (streaming front-line), 40% A100 (batch reranks). Routing policy would send streaming requests to H100 pool and batch jobs to A100 pool.

Sizing / reserved throughput guidance (ballpark):
- To achieve first-token p95 < 150ms and sustained token throughput for 22 concurrent streams at 350 tokens average: recommend reserved throughput ~14k tokens/sec (this provides headroom for bursts and longer sequences).
- For the worst-case 2,048 token sequences for up to 10% of traffic, we recommend autoscaling headroom or a small extra set of reserved instances (or routing longer sessions to a slightly degraded SLO pool).

Example configuration (starting point for POC):
- H100 pool: 4 x H100 nodes (each node configured to support ~4-6 concurrent streams at your model/quantization), reserved throughput target 8k tokens/sec.
- A100 pool: 6 x A100 nodes for batch rerank capacity and overflow, reserved throughput target 6k tokens/sec.
- Autoscaling: fast scale-up for sustained CPU/GPU utilization above 70% for >60s.

Tradeoffs:
- All-H100 will give the cleanest latency profile but costs ~25-40% more vs mixed depending on instance sizing and utilization.
- Mixed pools give strong cost-per-token benefits for batch work without compromising front-end p95 if routing/pinning is configured.

POC plan proposed (2 weeks):
1) Baseline: synthetic generator to mimic your token distribution + concurrency; run steady-state and burst tests.
2) Streaming first-byte/first-token latency tests (p50/p95/p99) across pools.
3) Long-sequence stress: send 2k+ token sequences to observe memory/KV behavior and fallback routing.
4) Report: consolidated p95 first-token, sustained tokens/sec, and infra cost estimate for monthly reserved commit.

I'll attach a short bench script and the initial sizing worksheet (attached to this thread). If you confirm the clarifying Qs above and sign off on the POC scope, we can spin up the test pools early next week.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
